extraction.Name: William Twiss
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent to his allotment at the time he received it, as he did not want to pay taxes on it, but that he was informed that it would be necessary for him to take it, so he did
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged 40 head of cattle and 200 head of horses, to the Security Savings Bank of Rapid City, South Dakota, for $4140.00; that there was a clause in this mortgage paper which included his 640 acres under the mortgage
extraction.Buyer: Security Savings Bank of Rapid City, South Dakota
extraction.Occupation/Income: only source of income is what he realizes by the boys farming the mother's allotment, and what he receives in the way of lease money from his own allotment
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; has poor health, being bothered with stomach trouble; wife's health is poor, she having rheumatism; has four boys at home ranging from 18 to 25 years of age, these boys working the mother's allotment and work for other people; in 1920 mortgaged 40 head of cattle and 200 head of horses for $4140.00 with a clause including his 640 acres, which he signed without knowing; in summer of 1928 bank claimed foreclosure, papers presented to wife of William Twiss to sign but she refused, and the foreclosure is not an accomplished fact; called at bank to get deed of trust back but received no satisfaction; has never received any help from the County or Government; file reference 04942, document page F.6
